First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+X-4 \\  & ={X}^{2}+X-4I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(B)={B}^{2}+B-4I.$

Let's calculate ${B}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(B):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(B) & ={B}^{2}+B-4I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2+0-4 & 6+2-0 \\ -3+(-1)-0 & 7+3-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
